findings.headline: Pricing page offers invoicing. FAQ says card only.
findings.explanation: An enterprise buyer doing diligence reads the FAQ and concludes you cannot invoice them.

claim_b.quote: Currently, you can pay only with a credit card. We plan to add more payment methods in the future.

findings.why_not_just_wording: One page sells invoicing as an Enterprise benefit, the other says no other payment method exists.
findings.caveat: The FAQ answer is probably about self-serve checkout, with invoicing arranged through sales. Neither page says so.

findings.headline: API concurrency is 10 on every paid plan. The comparison never says so.
findings.explanation: Rows scale from 3,000 to 1,000,000 across the tiers. API throughput does not move at all.

claim_b.quote: In Baserow Cloud, there's a limit of 10 concurrent API requests. This limit is subject to a fair use policy, and we reserve the right to lower it if it affects overall performance.

findings.why_not_just_wording: Every other usage dimension is listed by tier and this one is absent, so a reader cannot infer either the cap or that it never improves.
findings.caveat: Your pricing page carries a collapsed FAQ titled "What are the limitations in records, rows, and API requests?". We could read the heading, not the panel.

unusable_pages: https://baserow.io/signup and the subscription pages returned too little text to read
coverage_notes.what_was_not_checkable: The plan comparison on your pricing page is built from styled divs rather than a real table, so per-plan values lose their column alignment when flattened to text. Several rows publish three values for four plans, including row change history and application users. That may be a real gap or an artefact of the flattening, so we did not report it. The Premium plan advertises a free trial with no length stated on any page we read, and nothing says whether a card is required to start it.
